Dr Malcom Still

Rheumatologist

5 Grant St

Fairmont

03/05/2014

Dear Dr Still,

Re: Mr James Seymour                             DOB 19/09/1953

I am writing this letter to refer Mr Seymour, a 60-year-old retired academic, whose clinical features are
suggestive of gout. Your further assessment would be highly appreciated.

Mr Seymour is an ex-smoker. However, he is a heavy drinker. He has been suffering from regular attacks of    Comment [teacher1]: however
inflammation involving the first toe, for which he takes colchicine, indomethacin and allopurinol.           Comment [teacher2]: for many years,
Moreover, he has a family history of rheumatoid arthritis.

On 25/04/2014, the patient presented with a 4 – week history of a gouty attack, in which he experienced
pain and redness in the first left toe. Unfortunately, he was not compliant with the gout medications
because he thought that the main cause of his illness was rheumatoid arthritis. Consequently, he was
encouraged to take the regular gout treatment, paracetamol along with oxycodone. Additionally, he was
advised to decrease the intake of purine containing diet and alcohol. Finally, some investigations were
requested.

Today, regrettably, the ordered x-ray showed minor degenerative changes in the left first
metatarsophalangeal joint , while blood tests revealed mild hyperuricemia and a mildly elevated CRP level.
Accordingly, the treatment plane included an administration of allopurinol besides the dietary               Comment [teacher3]: plan
modification. Furthermore, a synovial fluid sample was recommended to be discussed with a                    Comment [teacher4]: better

rheumatologist.

In light of the above, the patient is being referred for further management. Should you have any queries,    episode. However, the patient insists on

please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor

Dr Malcom Still

5 Grant St

Fairmont

03/05/2014

Dear Dr Still,

Re: Mr James Seymour

DOB 19/09/1953

I am writing this letter to refer Mr Seymour, a 60-year-old retired academic, whose clinical features are
suggestive of gout. Your further assessment would be highly appreciated.

Mr Seymour is an ex-smoker. However, he is a heavy drinker. He has been suffering from regular attacks of
inflammation involving the first toe, for which he takes colchicine, indomethacin and allopurinol.
Moreover, he has a family history of rheumatoid arthritis.

Comment [teacher1]: however

Comment [teacher2]: for many years,

On 25/04/2014, the patient presented with a 4 – week history of a gouty attack, in which he experienced
pain and redness in the first left toe. Unfortunately, he was not compliant with the gout medications
because he thought that the main cause of his illness was rheumatoid arthritis. Consequently, he was
encouraged to take the regular gout treatment, paracetamol along with oxycodone. Additionally, he was
advised to decrease the intake of purine containing diet and alcohol. Finally, some investigations were
requested.

Today, regrettably, the ordered x-ray showed minor degenerative changes in the left first
metatarsophalangeal joint , while blood tests revealed mild hyperuricemia and a mildly elevated CRP level.
Accordingly, the treatment plane included an administration of allopurinol besides the dietary
modification. Furthermore, a synovial fluid sample was recommended to be discussed with a
rheumatologist.

In light of the above, the patient is being referred for further management. Should you have any queries,
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
